new_statements.rule_in_words: Both Ilorin descriptions (Mernyang dialect and Kofyar/Kwalla-Doemak dialect) analyse the language as a register-tone language with three level tones (H, M, L) carrying lexical contrast; neither assigns word stress to any position. The only remark touching stress is Olagbenro's generic contrast that the language 'operate[s] with tone rather than stress' (i.e. no contrastive stress is recognised). Netting 1967/1973 and Blench & Bulkaam 2019 (Jibyal) likewise give three level tones and say nothing about stress.
new_statements.exceptions: none; Sanni notes only a tonotactic restriction ('we cannot have a sequence of three high tones in a word'); Olagbenro describes tone deletion at morpheme boundaries.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone on isolated wordlist items (Ibadan 400 wordlist elicitation); no phrase-level prosody described apart from Anjorin's 'rising sentence-final intonation' in questions.
new_statements.identity_note: Olagbenro 2011 describes the Mernyang (Mirriam) variety, Glottolog dialect mirr1240 under Pan [kofy1242] (informant from Kwa, Qua'an Pan LGA). Sanni 2011 describes 'Kofyar' with informants from the Kwalla/Doemak area of Qua'an Pan LGA (Kofyar-Doemak dimm1243 / Kwagallak kwag1238). Netting 1967/1973 is Kofyar of Bong village (Kofyar hills), which Blench equates with Doemak. Blench & Bulkaam 2019 is Jibyal, Glottolog dialect jiby1234 under Pan. Nteng [nqt, nucl1698] and Jakattoe [jrt] are separate Glottolog languages and were not used.

sources.note: Sec. 2.2-2.3: after illustrating English noun/verb stress pairs, 'Unlike English language, African languages operate with tone rather than stress.. Mernyang language attest 3 levels of tone which are high tone, mid tone, and low tone. Tone.. brings difference in the meaning of a words just as stress brings a change in meaning to words in English language.' Ch. 4: registered (level) tones H, L, M, co-occurrence, lexical function, tone deletion at morpheme boundary. No statement of stress placement. Informant from Kwa (Mernyang).

sources.note: Nothing language-specific. Sec. 3.5 'Tones in Kofyar Language': 'Kofyar is a tone language.. primarily a register tone language.. Kofyar language falls under the discrete level tone. The tones in Kofyar are: High tone, Mid tone, Low tone'; tone is lexical (minimal pairs gyará 'hawk' / gyàrá 'dance'); 'we cannot have a sequence of three high tones in a word'. Stress appears only in generic textbook definitions of the syllable (Ladefoged/Hyman). Informants from the Kwalla/Doemak area of Qua'an Pan LGA.
